scores.why: Per-phoneme GOP over a curated confusion set on an LM-free wav2vec2 phoneme CTC model (server/app/scoring/gop.py) so substitutions aren't auto-corrected, plus per-child threshold calibration from therapist overrides (calibration.py), phonemizer-validated LLM word suggestions (llm/validators.py) and self-QA of ElevenLabs audio with the own scorer. Speech-therapy apps exist, but explicit 'heard S instead of SZ' for Polish is a fresh angle.

Hits nearly every brief point: README 'Gdzie jest AI' table shows the AI's role and component fit, docs explain technical decisions and limits, and user control is concrete (niepewne verdict, confidence, per-attempt playback, therapist override in AttemptsTable.tsx) with one concrete use case (Zosia practising SZ).

Addresses a real gap (home practice between weekly therapy sessions, therapist-driven, local audio, no child name sent to the LLM), but only SZ and R are covered, eval/results.md is 1 adult imitating errors (no children), and it requires a local Python server with a 1.2 GB model.

Screenshots show a polished, consistent child app (custom animated lynx mascot, lesson path, mouth-position hint, no punishments) and a professional therapist dashboard with a sound × position heatmap and per-attempt table; mobile layouts too.

~9.4k real LOC across a React front end and a FastAPI server, 60 tests (server/tests), a reproducible eval harness and a live-session write-up; however the Claude path ran only from a hand-written cache, eval recordings are gitignored, and the live demo is down.

projects.built_during_event: yes — PLAN.md dated 4.10 04:30, model check 04.10 ~05:40; one squashed commit at 10:25 CEST (before the 11:00 deadline), plus a README demo-link commit at 12:54 CEST
strengths: Real phoneme-level scoring: GOP-CTC over a confusion set plus its own forced alignment and spectral-centroid gate; 0% false alarms on clean audio in its own evaluation
Strong human-in-the-loop: unsure verdict, per-attempt playback, therapist overrides that recalibrate per child, approval queue for AI-suggested words
All LLM paths (live, cache, templates) pass the same validators: phonemizer checks, numbers must match the data, banned-word list
Unusually honest limitations; privacy choices: local scoring, camera stays in the browser, no emotion recognition
Polished child UI and clean therapist dashboard
weaknesses: Evaluation is 52 clips from one adult imitating errors; no child speech; interdental lisp is often not identified
Only SZ and R are implemented
The Claude features never ran live during the event (no API key)
Needs a local Python server with a 1.2 GB model, which makes family deployment hard
red_flags: The Claude 'responses' in server/data/llm_cache were hand-written by Claude Code, not produced by the model (disclosed and labelled in the UI)
One squashed commit hides the development timeline
Most code was generated by parallel Claude Code agents from a Claude-written PLAN.md in about 6 hours (disclosed)
Child-flow screenshots use simulated scoring (labelled 'Tryb pokazowy')
projects.verdict: A mature, well-justified AI-for-a-real-need prototype with real phoneme scoring, honest evaluation, thorough human control and polished design, held back by adult-only validation and an LLM path never run live.

calibration_note: Absolute scale: well above a typical hackathon prototype, kept below 9 by the lack of child-speech validation, the cache-only LLM path, and fully agent-generated code in one squashed commit.
